//: Downstream hosts are Docker Compose SERVICE NAMES, not IP addresses and not
localhost. Docker's embedded DNS resolves 'invoice-service' to whichever
container currently holds that name on the pandapocket network. That is this
system's service discovery: containers can be stopped, rebuilt and replaced
with a different IP and the gateway needs no reconfiguration.
This file is the deployed truth. ocelot.Development.json overrides the hosts
with localhost and published ports for running the gateway outside Docker.
Rate limiting and the API key authentication handler are added on days 4 and 6.

//RateLimitOptions: Client identity comes from X-Merchant-Id, which the gateway sets itself
after validating the API key, so the quota is per MERCHANT rather than
per key or per IP. A merchant with three keys shares one quota, which is
the honest unit: the limit protects the platform from one customer, not
from one credential. Per-IP would lump every merchant behind a corporate
NAT into a single bucket.
Limits apply to the invoice write path only. Rates are public market data
that a checkout page polls legitimately every few seconds.
Every route carries an explicit RateLimitOptions block, including the
ones that are not limited. That is not verbosity for its own sake: with a
global ClientIdHeader set, Ocelot applies a default empty rule to any
route that does not opt out, then cannot identify the client and answers
503. Setting EnableRateLimiting false explicitly is what keeps the public
routes public. This was found on day 7 after it had silently broken
/api/rates, /api/auth/login and /api/checkout for a whole day.
Note the gap this leaves: unauthenticated requests are rejected by the
API key middleware before Ocelot ever sees them, so they carry no
X-Merchant-Id and are never rate limited here. Someone brute forcing keys
is throttled by nothing at this layer. Every rejection is logged as
API_KEY_INVALID with its source address, so the SOC layer can see it, but
detection is not prevention and the report says so.

RateLimitOptions.QuotaExceededMessage: Rate limit exceeded. Slow down and retry after the period resets.

//RequestIdKey: Ocelot generates a request id under this header when one is absent and
propagates it downstream. It is pointed at the same header the services
already use, so the gateway becomes the place correlation ids originate
and every service downstream sees an id that is already present.

//ServiceDiscovery: Routes name a SERVICE, not a host and port. Ocelot asks Consul which
instances are registered under that name and healthy, and load balances
This is the difference between discovery and configuration. Compose DNS
resolved a name to a container whether or not that container could serve a
request; Consul only returns instances whose health check is passing, so
an instance whose database has gone away is removed from rotation.
